title: Custom business apps
seoTitle: Custom Business Apps & Internal Tools | EFIops
metaDescription: Purpose-built planning tools, operational applications and portals. EFIops develops business software around your workflow, data and users.
h1: Your process deserves a better tool.
eyebrow: Custom applications · Built around your team
lead: If your working day depends on copied cells, extra tabs and knowing which file is current, there may be a better way. Build a focused planning tool, portal or operational screen that fits the job.

sections.heading: You shouldn't need five workarounds to complete one job.
paragraphs: A plan lives in one spreadsheet. Actual results come from another system. Staff requirements are calculated elsewhere. People copy the same information between tools and lose track of which version is current.
A custom application can connect the relevant information and give each person a clear view of the work they need to do.

sections.heading: Build the tool your workflow is missing.
items: Planning and scheduling tools. Work with forecasts, capacity, staffing and operational requirements.
Internal portals. Give teams a clearer way to enter, review and manage information.
Operational dashboards. Combine current status with the actions people need to take.
Customer or supplier interfaces. Scope a controlled portal for an agreed exchange of information.
Existing app improvements. Add a missing feature, improve usability or connect an application to another system.

sections.heading: Prove the important workflow first.
paragraphs: We map the users, the information and the steps the application needs to support. A first version focuses on the core workflow, with access rules and data handling included in the design.
Testing uses realistic tasks rather than only checking whether the screens look right. The handover covers the application, its dependencies and options for maintaining it.

faqs.question: Can you work on an existing React application?
faqs.answer: Yes. React and JavaScript are part of Karol's practical development experience. We inspect the codebase and current architecture before agreeing changes.

faqs.question: Can the app use our existing database?
faqs.answer: Often, through a suitable API or integration. Access, performance and the data's structure need to be considered.

faqs.question: Should we build an app or use an existing product?
faqs.answer: That is a discovery question. If a suitable existing product solves the problem well, custom development may not be necessary.

faqs.question: Can we add AI later?
faqs.answer: Potentially. A clear data model, permission system and API make it easier to evaluate a useful AI feature without rebuilding the whole application.

cta.label: Discuss your application
cta.heading: What is your team working around?
cta.text: Show us the spreadsheets, screens or steps that make the job harder than it needs to be.

primaryIntent: custom business application developer; internal tools development.
summary: Bring plans, records and actions into an application built for the way your team works.

useCases.title: What happens if another order comes in?
useCases.body: Change the volume, compare the hours required with available staffing, and see which part of the plan needs reviewing.

useCases.title: One place for the current status.
useCases.body: Give each role the records and actions it needs. Keep updates attached to the work instead of scattered across inboxes.

useCases.title: A clearer way to exchange information.
useCases.body: Scope a controlled portal for requests, documents or progress updates, with the access rules designed around the users.

journey.heading: From an awkward spreadsheet to a plan the team can act on.
journey.example: A packing team needs to see whether next week’s orders fit its available hours.
journey.question: Can the team cover the workload?
journey.boundary: Payroll, shift scheduling and stock control need their own agreed scope.

stages.label: Understand
stages.title: Watch how the plan is made today.
stages.body: We follow the spreadsheet, the copied inputs and the decisions made from it. We ask who edits the plan, which values change and where a missing or outdated input can mislead the team.
stages.output: A workflow map, input inventory and user roles.

stages.label: Agree
stages.title: Agree the calculation and the first screen.
stages.body: The first planner uses units, handling time and actual available hours. Four minutes per unit and 32 hours per person make the workload visible. We agree validation, account access and the delivery scope.
stages.output: A focused screen specification and calculation rules.

stages.label: Build
stages.title: Build around the decision the team makes.
stages.body: The team reviews a working planner with editable demand and staffing. Required hours and capacity update together, making it easier to discuss the gap instead of rebuilding the spreadsheet.
stages.output: A reviewable planning screen and validated inputs.

stages.label: Test
stages.title: Check the numbers at the edges as well as the centre.
stages.body: We verify known workloads, demand above capacity, input limits and relevant access controls. A useful planner should explain a shortfall clearly and keep invalid inputs out of the calculation.
stages.output: Calculation checks, input validation and user-flow results.

stages.label: Hand over
stages.title: Hand over the tool and the assumptions.
stages.body: The team learns how to enter the plan, interpret the result and update agreed assumptions. The handover covers hosting, accounts, data ownership and any ongoing support arrangement.
stages.output: A user guide, assumption record and ownership plan.

tests.label: Another person
tests.reason: Capacity becomes 128 hours; workload stays at 120.

handover.title: Everyday tasks
handover.body: Entering demand, updating staffing and interpreting the capacity result.

handover.title: Assumptions & data
handover.body: Handling time, available hours, input ownership and storage requirements.

handover.title: Running the application
handover.body: Hosting, access, maintenance and the separately agreed support route.
